transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-01-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (Clarion Head of AI), Dev Patel (Clarion Platform Eng), Laura Kim (Clarion Security)

Summary:
Quick scoping for a 4-6 week POC to evaluate Redwood for Clarion's clinical summarization and triage workload. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, quality regession limits), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and decision criteria across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Compliance and VPC/KMS needs flagged as blockers for production.

Topics:
- Workload profile: concurrent users, sequence lengths, average tokens per request
- Performance targets: p50/p95 latency, throughput
- Cost targets and unit economics
- Security/compliance: HIPAA-ish requirements, SOC2, KMS, audit logs
- Timeline: POC, pilot, production rollout
- Decision criteria: latency vs cost vs data residency

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:08] Sara Lopez: hi this is sara, head of ai at clarion, we run clinical summarization and patient triage, concerned about PHI and latency for triage flows
[00:16] Dev Patel: dev here, platform team - we own infra and onboarding, want predictable costs and VPC support
[00:22] Laura Kim: laura from security - mainly compliance questions and key mgmt, we have HIPAA obligations
[00:30] Maya Chen: great, ill run through a proposed POC plan then ethan will cover performance/benchmark approach, and we can tee up decision criteria for hosted/dedicated/private
[00:45] Ethan Park: hey all, quick note: i may mumbly at points, if something sounds odd shout up, i'll cover batching, kv cache, quantization paths and what we typically measure

[01:10] Sara Lopez: our main success criteria: 1) p95 latency under 350ms for summaries up to ~512 tokens, 2) throughput of ~200 rps during peak batch windows, 3) cost target below our internal threshold (~$X per 1M tokens), 4) no regressions in summary accuracy (>95% pass on our eval prompts)
[01:35] Maya Chen: good, thats clear; we usually structure POC to hit those exactly - start hosted for speed, run benchmarks, then decide if dedicated or private needed based on latency and compliance
[01:50] Dev Patel: question - whats the timeline for private? we can't have PHI leave our VPC for prod, so private likely required for long term; hosted ok for POC if data is synthetic, but private onboarding historically takes months
[02:06] Ethan Park: yes correct, private (we call privet sometimes in notes) typically 6-10 weeks for on-prem or VPC-private control plane, dedicated is faster - usually 2-3 weeks to get reserved pools up, hosted you can start within days
[02:25] Laura Kim: for compliance we need customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 7 years, SAML SSO and RBAC, and SOC2 evidence. Does Redwood support those?
[02:40] Maya Chen: we do SOC2, we have KMS integration and can support customer-managed keys for Private; for Dedicated we can provide VPC peering and customer key options - i'll attach the SOC2 summary and KMS notes after the call

[03:05] Ethan Park: on perf, couple of notes - model choice and quantization impact latency big time. For e.g., a 7B quantized model with torch kernels gives much lower cost but p95 can vary; batching and prefix KV-cache for conversational flows will save a lot if you have repeated prefixes
[03:30] Dev Patel: our workload: about 200 concurrent agents during peak, average sequence length ~480 tokens, average output 120 tokens, predicted throughput target 200 rps during business hours, burst to 500 for triage spikes
[03:50] Ethan Park: ok that maps. for sizing we typically estimate GPU hours by tokens/sec * concurrency; for 200 rps with 512 context you might start with 2-4 A10x or A100 equivalent for dedicated, but we will run benchmarks with your traces to confirm

[04:12] Sara Lopez: quality is also huge - we will run our eval set (1k prompts) and expect no more than 5% regression vs our baseline model. how do you handle model rollbacks?
[04:25] Maya Chen: rollouts are integrated in the console - can do canary traffic, A/B, and automatic fallback to a warm-compatible variant if we see regressions or latency spikes

[04:40] Dev Patel: cost math - how do you show token-level breakdown? we need per-route cost so product managers can forecast
[04:50] Maya Chen: console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards. for POC we'll run a few benchmark runs and produce a per-scenario cost estimate; we'll include batching and cache assumptions so its apples-to-apples

[05:10] Laura Kim: about data residency - Clarion requires that PHI stays in our cloud region, and logs with PHI masked. can Redwood ensure region pinning?
[05:22] Ethan Park: region pinning is supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted can be region-limited depending on our infra but may not meet strict residency for PHI; Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full control over region and network boundary

[05:45] Sara Lopez: ok seems like decision tree: start with hosted for quick benchmark if we can mask data, run evals; if latency or residency fails, move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC peering; if PHI in prod then Private is required but longer lead time

[06:05] Maya Chen: exactly. for the POC we propose: week 0-1: plan + access, week 2: deploy hosted test harness + run baseline benchmarks, week 3: tune batching/quant configs and rerun, week 4: run full eval suite and present results; after that we can decide dedicated pilot or private kickoff

[06:30] Dev Patel: whats involved in the benchmark run from our side? we can provide traces and sample containers, do you need S3 access or a VPN?
[06:40] Ethan Park: S3 or pre-signed URLs for dataset is easiest; for private tests we may need VPN or peered VPC. for hosted we'll take sanitized traces. also need a small subset of real traffic to validate distribution, but agreed sanitized or synthetic for initial pass

[07:05] Laura Kim: security notes - we require SAML SSO, RBAC roles for platform, detailed audit logs, and attestation of encryption at rest for any logs; also KMS for keys. is there an incurring fee for dedicated KMS?
[07:20] Maya Chen: there can be minor infra pass-throughs for HSM/KMS depending on provider, but we will call that out in the pricing sheet. Dedicated and Private give stronger KMS options; hosted offers managed keys unless you move to private key control

[07:40] Sara Lopez: what about fallback policies if capacity is constrained? we cannot have triage go offline
[07:48] Ethan Park: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants (lower cost / lower perf) and cross-region failover; you can configure safe-fallback sequences and escalation alerts

[08:10] Dev Patel: curious about monitoring hooks - we need traces, token-level costs, and latency histograms. can you export to our Datadog/Prometheus?
[08:20] Maya Chen: yes, we have tracing hooks and can export metrics to Datadog/Prometheus, plus webhooks for alerts. we'll include sample dashboards in the POC deck

[08:40] Sara Lopez: on benchmarks - what metrics will you deliver? p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1M tokens, error rates, and quality eval results?
[08:50] Ethan Park: yes those plus a sensitivity analysis across batch sizes, quantization, and model variants. we'll provide a spreadsheet with scenario cost breakdowns and recommended config for production

[09:10] Maya Chen: i'll send POC plan + pricing, ethan sends benchmark scripts, clarion provides traces/dataset, then we run week-of-19 benchmarks. if results hit your targets we'll scope dedicated pilot; if compliance requires, we'll kick private onboarding timeline in parallel

[09:35] Laura Kim: if we need private, what are the prerequisites? we need HSM/KMS integration plan, network diagrams, and a security review timeline
[09:45] Maya Chen: we'll assemble an onboarding packet for Private that includes network checklist, KMS/HSM integration steps, audit log retention options, and estimated timeline (6-10 weeks), plus a point-of-contact at Redwood

[10:05] Dev Patel: can you share any prior healthcare POC wins or references?
[10:10] Maya Chen: yes we'll include two anonymized references and a short case study of a healthcare customer who moved from hosted to dedicated then to private for PHI workloads

[10:30] Sara Lopez: last question on pricing - do you charge for benchmark runs?
[10:35] Maya Chen: initial POC benchmarking is usually included as part of the trial; long-running dedicated capacity or private integration costs are quoted separately in the POC pricing sheet

[10:50] Ethan Park: small technical gotcha: watch out for KV cache priming for the triage flow; if your prompts share prefixes you will see big gains on throughput and cost once caching is enabled

[11:10] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up - recap of next steps and action items, we'll aim to have the doc pack to you by monday the 11th

[11:30] Sara Lopez: thanks all, this is helpful. looking forward to the benchmark run
[11:35] Dev Patel: thanks, we'll get traces and dataset over by the 14th
[11:40] Laura Kim: thanks - i'll send compliance checklist and key requirements by the 12th
[11:45] Maya Chen: great, i'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark run and share the POC deck and SOC2 artifacts

Questions:
- Laura: is Private the only option for PHI in prod? (answer: typically yes, or dedicated with strict VPC peering and controls but many customers choose Private)
- Dev: what GPU types will you recommend? (answer: depends on model/quant; A10/A100 class typically for throughput needs)

End of transcript.
